body_ar: تخصصات العلوم الإسلامية التي اشتغل بها العلماء كثيرة، ومن تعلمها، فوصل إلى حد متوسط من إدراكها، واستطاع تدريس كل واحد من هذه العلوم فهو (العالم)، ومن تخصص في بعضها لم يستحق هذا اللقب، وإنما يستحق أن يدرج في حملة العلم والمتخصصين في بعض جوانبه دون بعض. وعلى طلاب العلم أن يعطوا هذا العلم حقه من الاهتمام والعناية، وأن يحرصوا على آدابه ووسائله وشروطه، وأن يستشعروا فضله ومزيته. العلم والآداب: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين، وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه لطلب العلم، وبعد: العناصر التي سأتحدث عنها في هذا الدرس هي: العنصر الأول: فضل العلم وأهله. العنصر الثاني: أجر طلب العلم وتعليمه. العنصر الثالث: الكتب العلمية وفضلها. العنصر الرابع: شروط طلب العلم. العنصر الخامس: وسائل تحصيل العلم. العنصر السادس: أنواع العلوم. ......
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* The specialisms of the Islamic sciences with which scholars have occupied themselves are many. Whoever has learned them, has reached a middling degree of grasp of them, and is able to teach each one of these sciences — he is "the scholar". Whoever has specialised in some of them does not merit this title; he merits only to be counted among the bearers of knowledge, and among those who specialise in some of its aspects and not others. Students of knowledge must give this knowledge its due of concern and attention, must be keen upon its proprieties, its means and its conditions, and must be conscious of its merit and its distinction.

## Knowledge and the proprieties

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Mercy-Giving. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds. I ask God's blessing and peace upon the one sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions, and upon all who have taken guidance from his guidance in the seeking of knowledge. And now: the elements I shall speak about in this lesson are:

The first element: the merit of knowledge and of its people.
The second element: the reward for seeking knowledge and for teaching it.
The third element: scholarly books and their merit.
The fourth element: the conditions of seeking knowledge.
The fifth element: the means of acquiring knowledge.
The sixth element: the kinds of the sciences.

......

flags.note: CRITICAL for display, and the purest instance of style guide section 9 in this slice. What survives of the lesson itself is a table of contents and nothing more: six announced elements, not one of which is addressed, followed by six dots. A reader arriving at a page titled 'The Proprieties of Seeking Knowledge' would find a list of six headings and no content whatever. Everything of substance on the page is the site's synopsis, which is not the Sheikh's words. This record must carry a prominent excerpt banner or be suppressed.

flags.note: A consequential and contestable claim — that the title of 'scholar' belongs only to one able to teach every one of the Islamic sciences, and that a specialist does not merit it — and it falls entirely inside the site's synopsis. The transcribed portion of the lesson contains not one word of it. Given who the Sheikh is, an English page saying this under his name would be read as his definition and quoted as such, so the attribution must be visible. The parentheses around 'the scholar' are the source's own and mark it as a title being defined; the English uses quotation marks for the same effect.

flags.note: Every other record in this run of thirteen closes the formula with 'and followed his practice until the Day of Judgement'. This one instead has 'in the seeking of knowledge', which fits the lesson's subject but departs from the template. It may be the Sheikh adapting the formula to his topic, or a transcription loss. Rendered exactly as served and not restored, per style guide section 6.

translator_notes: One of a run of thirteen records, IDs 688-700, all uploaded on 5 and 8-9 May 2011 within a few hours of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/c-a-* series. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lessons were delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.
This is the last record of the run and of this slice. It is also the emptiest: of its 821 source characters, the greater part is the site's synopsis.
'آداب' is rendered 'proprieties' — the manners and disciplines proper to an activity — rather than 'etiquette', which is too slight for what the term carries here.
No ruling term appears anywhere in the record.
